description: Canonical search response-quality scenarios for release-specific SQL, index lifecycle, and compatibility.

evals.name: fulltext-ranking
evals.prompt:
In YDB 26.2.1.14, articles has id Uint64 as its primary key, body Utf8, and a
fulltext_plain index ft_idx on body. This query fails:
  SELECT id, FulltextScore(body, $q) AS score
  FROM articles
  WHERE score > 0 OR FulltextMatch(body, $q)
  ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10;
I want BM25 results matching at least half of the optional query terms.
The analyzer produces three optional terms for this request.
The query text has no + prefixes; preserve those term semantics.
Give the corrected index choice and parameterized SQL. Do not execute it.
evals.expected_output: Corrected parameterized BM25 query with the relevance index, VIEW, and preserved optional-term semantics.
expectations:
Require fulltext_relevance for BM25 and show a query through that index
using VIEW. Repeat the identical FulltextScore expression in SELECT and
WHERE ... > 0, with "Or" AS DefaultOperator and a valid string
MinimumShouldMatch threshold requiring two of the three analyzed optional
terms, for example "2" or an explicitly bound string parameter with that
value. Accept an equivalent valid threshold. Explain that
percentage thresholds round down: "50%" permits only one of three analyzed
optional terms and does not meet the requested at-least-half condition.
The concrete ceil(3 / 2) = 2 explanation is sufficient; a general formula
for other term counts is optional. Do not use the SELECT alias in WHERE or combine scoring
with FulltextMatch via SQL OR. Sort the score descending. Distinguish
query-term Or semantics from SQL OR around full-text predicates. Bind the
query text as a parameter. Do not add + prefixes or require a mandatory
term: with Or and no +, all supplied terms are optional and MinimumShouldMatch
applies to all of them.

evals.name: hybrid-candidates
evals.prompt:
On a YDB server with HybridRank enabled, documents has primary key id Uint64,
body Utf8 and embedding String containing 768-dimensional FloatVectors.
Ready indexes are ft_a and ft_b (both fulltext_relevance on body), and vec_idx
(vector_kmeans_tree, cosine, on embedding). Write SQL using ft_b with 100 text
candidates, 200 vector candidates, vector weight 2, text weight 1, and final
result count $limit. The query text and encoded vector are parameters.
Explain the three different limits/probing controls. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: A valid native hybrid query with explicit per-branch candidate limits, distinct probing controls, and tenant scoping preserved.
expectations:
Read documents without VIEW. Use HybridRank as the entire ORDER BY key with
a FulltextScore branch and cosine Knn branch. Use positionally matching
Weights, Indexes selecting ft_b and vec_idx, and Limits selecting 100 and 200.
Bind query text, binary String query vector, and outer $limit. Do not copy
the standalone WHERE FulltextScore > 0 into the hybrid query or add another
sort key. Set KMeansTreeSearchTopSize explicitly. Explain that it controls
vector probing, Limits controls candidates before fusion, and the outer
LIMIT controls output rows. Explicit Limits permits parameterized LIMIT.
evals.covers: Search · Hybrid branch selection and parameterized limit

evals.name: hybrid-compatibility
evals.prompt:
We use YDB 26.3.1.16 RC with its default features and PRIMARY KEY (tenant, id).
I want native HybridRank with
full-text ON (tenant, body) and vector ON (tenant, embedding), always filtered
to tenant = $tenant. The versioned docs have a page for every feature.
After addressing the primary key, can I extend the vector index to
ON (tenant, region, embedding) while filtering only tenant? Explain the
schema, index, and feature requirements before giving deployable DDL.
Preserve tenant scoping.
evals.expected_output: Exact-RC enablement, single-column hybrid primary-key, and branch-specific prefix requirements, preserving tenant scoping without unsafe DDL.
expectations:
Explain that 26.3.1.16 RC lists native hybrid search, filtered full-text
indexes, and arbitrary full-text primary keys as disabled by default;
feature pages alone do not establish enablement. The exact RC optimizer
requires a single-column primary key, so the supplied (tenant, id) key
cannot run native hybrid even if arbitrary full-text keys are enabled.
Do not infer RC composite-key support from upstream main or full-text
arbitrary-key support. If newer implementations are discussed, distinguish
them from this RC without inventing a released patch boundary. A separately designed single-key
search table, a verified newer build, or application-side fusion can be
proposed without executing a destructive key migration.
Distinguish the 26.3 documentation's exclusion of prefixed vector indexes
from the exact RC's source-verified behavior: with hybrid enabled and a
single-column primary key, vector branches accept equality on a nonempty
contiguous leading prefix. ON (tenant, region, embedding) therefore accepts
tenant = $tenant in this RC; do not require region as well or reject the
prefix solely from the guide. The full-text branch requires equality on
every prefix column, plus enabled filtered full-text and compact relevance
support. Do not generalize the RC prefix rule to all versions. Preserve
tenant scoping; do not silently remove the filter. Verify enablement and ready
indexes before native execution. Do not present deployable DDL for the
unsupported supplied key or assumed feature enablement. No cluster configuration
change or destructive schema migration should be executed.
evals.covers: Search · YDB 26.3 hybrid enablement and prefix compatibility

evals.name: vector-lifecycle
evals.prompt:
On YDB 25.1, I plan to create an empty documents table with a vector_kmeans_tree
cosine index, BulkUpsert a million 768-dimensional float embeddings, then
query ORDER BY Knn::CosineDistance(embedding, $q) DESC LIMIT 10 without VIEW.
The index covers only title. A teammate says SQL UPSERT after the build will
always keep ANN results fresh. Fix the plan, explain how to assess recall and
handle continued writes, and tell me whether the fulltext/hybrid examples
apply to this release. Write guidance only.
evals.expected_output: A corrected YDB 25.1 vector loading and query plan, with release-specific update limits and a meaningful recall baseline.
expectations:
The answer must load representative data before building the vector index,
and place BulkUpsert before index creation because synchronous indexes do
not support it. Verify vector-index availability and the exact 25.1 build;
introduction is documented in 25.1.2.7 RC. Do not promise later writes are
supported or automatically reflected in the 25.1 index: the guide warns
that updates need rebuilding, and the DDL page also warns against mutations.
Require target verification or use an unindexed/exact-search or validated
rebuild workflow for changing data. It must show indexed search with
VIEW, cosine distance ascending, an explicit KMeansTreeSearchTopSize, and
an encoded binary String query vector matching dimension 768. Covering the
embedding as well as title avoids the vector lookup. Recall should be
compared with an exact baseline using the same filters. Do not prescribe
fulltext indexes or native HybridRank as documented 25.1 capabilities.
evals.covers: Search · YDB 25.1 vector lifecycle and recall
